label: GLOBAL TRADE
voice_script: In March 2021, a single ship brought global trade to its knees. The Ever Given, a vessel longer than the Eiffel Tower is tall, became hopelessly wedged across the Suez Canal, one of the planet's most vital arteries. The result? A traffic jam of over 400 ships and a staggering economic toll: ten billion dollars... per day. For six tense days, the world watched as a tiny excavator, and later a fleet of powerful tugboats, battled to free the giant. It took a Supermoon high tide and a monumental effort to finally break the deadlock. The incident was a stunning reminder of how a single point of failure can threaten the entire global supply chain.

screens.clip_moment: The small yellow excavator digging sand away from the bow of the massive container ship.

screens.text: ...was the first attempt to move this.
screens.clip_description: Ever Given stuck Suez Canal aerial view
screens.clip_moment: High aerial drone shot revealing the entire 400m ship wedged completely from bank to bank.

screens.text: A 400-meter ship blocking 12% of world trade.
screens.clip_description: Ever Given stuck Suez Canal aerial view
screens.clip_moment: A shot looking down the length of the ship, showing thousands of containers stacked high.

screens.text: Creating a 400-ship traffic jam visible from space.
screens.clip_moment: Satellite view showing a massive queue of ships in the Red Sea and Mediterranean.

screens.text: It took a fleet of 14 tugboats...
screens.clip_moment: Multiple tugboats surrounding the stern of the Ever Given, pushing and pulling against the massive hull.

screens.text: ...and the pull of a Supermoon high tide.
screens.clip_moment: The moment the ship begins to visibly move and straighten in the canal, with tugboats celebrating with horns and water cannons.

screens.text: One ship. Six days. Global chaos.
